issues.description: The template's Farm.singFarmSongVerse method signature has its Animal parameter commented out (no parameter), while the problem statement UML and the solution implementation define singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This mismatch in method signature can confuse students about how verses should receive the animal to sing and prevents directly adopting the intended implementation from the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the parameter in the template method signature to match the specification: change private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) and update the method body accordingly so students can implement the verse logic per-animal.

issues.description: The template Main.java (commented-out example code) calls farm.feed(), but the problem statement and solution use and require feedAllAnimals() as the Farm method name. The mismatched method name in the example can mislead students about the correct API to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the example code in template Main.java to call the correct method name (farm.feedAllAnimals()) to match the problem statement and solution, or alternatively change the task specification to accept feed() if that naming was intended.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution define the Farm method as feedAllAnimals(), but the template's Main.java calls farm.feed(). This uses a different identifier for the same conceptual operation (feeding all animals) and can confuse students about which method to implement or call, potentially leading to compilation errors or wasted time searching for a missing method.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the call in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java from farm.feed() to farm.feedAllAnimals(), or add a feed() method in Farm that delegates to feedAllAnimals() so the template and problem/solution use the same identifier.
